clue.text: You can hear it's beating time in Spring

indicators.note: hearing something points to how the phrase sounds when spoken, not how it is written

blocks.note: to lam is to thrash, so lamming season would be a period of beatings

explanation.surface: A musician keeps the beat as spring arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: LAM is an old slang verb meaning to beat; the B of LAMBING is silent, so the two phrases sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Ewes give birth to their young mostly in early spring, so farmers call those weeks lambing season.

clue.text: No star orbiting, nothing heard from unearthly traveller

indicators.note: something orbiting is going round and round, so these letters are spun into a new order
heard tells us to take the word for nothing by its sound rather than its spelling

blocks.note: the letters of these two words, rearranged
aught is an old word for zero, a variant of naught

explanation.surface: No star is in orbit and nothing is heard from a lone traveller beyond Earth.
explanation.walkthrough: The homophone is loose: AUGHT (nothing) is said like the last syllable of the answer, ASTRONAUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A spaceman travels away from the planet, so his journeys are literally out of this world.

clue.text: Footwear: final day to plunder

indicators.note: final asks for only the closing letter of the word that follows

blocks.note: a boot is a kind of footwear
the last letter of day

explanation.surface: A pirate pulls on his boots on the last day before raiding.
explanation.definitionFit: Booty is goods seized by force, the same spoils that plunder names as a noun.

clue.text: No alternative, so I go in lower down

indicators.note: go in says one piece enters inside the other piece

blocks.note: nether means lower, as in the nether regions
taken as written

explanation.surface: With no other option, I must climb down further.
explanation.walkthrough: I sits after the first two letters of NETHER to make NEITHER.
explanation.definitionFit: Neither, as in 'neither option', rejects both choices, leaving no alternative at all.

clue.text: Hush fairy folk with mothballs

blocks.note: sh is the sound used to ask for quiet
elves are small magical beings of folklore

explanation.surface: Someone quietens a crowd of fairies carrying mothballs.
explanation.walkthrough: Mothballs is a verb here, not the moth-repelling balls of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To mothball a plan is to put it aside indefinitely, just as one shelves it.

clue.text: Oh, Papa, cry freely for books lost from the bible

indicators.note: freely means without constraint, so the letters are let loose into any order

blocks.note: the letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A child sobs openly to Dad about lost scriptures.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apocrypha are writings left out of the accepted canon of scripture, removed from many editions.

clue.text: Not in the party to come first

blocks.note: out is the opposite of in
a do is an informal word for a party

explanation.surface: Someone missed the party and wants to arrive first next time.
explanation.definitionFit: To outdo rivals is to beat them, finishing ahead in any contest.

clue.text: Tricky time of the month, the "cruelest" one to clowns from dawn to dusk

blocks.note: T. S. Eliot's The Waste Land opens 'April is the cruellest month'
clowns and fools are both jesters
the daylight hours

explanation.surface: A wry remark that the harshest month belongs to jesters all day long.
explanation.definitionFit: On the first of April people play pranks and hoaxes, so it is a day of trickery.

clue.text: Newest technology from California, for example, preposterous to Father

indicators.note: preposterous means absurd and out of order, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: California is one of the US states
the letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Dad finds the latest gadgets from California absurd.
explanation.definitionFit: State-of-the-art describes the most advanced, up-to-date equipment or methods available.

clue.text: Lord it over others? Points are lost!

indicators.note: lost suggests letters gone astray and scattered, ending up in a different order

blocks.note: the letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A smug player gloats as the opponents drop points.
explanation.definitionFit: To patronise is to treat people with condescension, acting superior as a lord might.

clue.text: Group of musicians get alien after a month

indicators.note: after places one piece behind the other in the order of writing

blocks.note: OCT is the calendar abbreviation for October
ET is the extra-terrestrial of the film

explanation.surface: A band signs up a space creature a month later.
explanation.definitionFit: An octet is an ensemble of eight players or singers.

clue.text: Press centre of eye - it's a mockery

indicators.note: centre of asks for only the middle letter of the following word

blocks.note: to iron clothes is to press them
the middle letter of eye

explanation.surface: Pushing on the middle of someone's eye would be a cruel joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Irony says the opposite of what is meant, often as a form of ridicule or mockery.

clue.text: Hang about! Drink is found in transport dock

blocks.note: to hover is to linger or hang around
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: Someone loiters at the docks where drinking goes on.
explanation.walkthrough: A hoverport is a terminal for hovercraft, such as the old cross-Channel services from Dover.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoverport is the terminal where hovercraft load and unload passengers, a dock for that craft.

clue.text: Sweet-talk and more, even!

blocks.note: first meaning: to praise insincerely
second meaning: comparative of flat, more level

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is read as flat-ter, smoother or more level, not as the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to compliment someone excessively, and the adjective form means more level or smooth.

clue.text: Shape of a bone in the base of the thumb

definitions.text: a bone in the base of the thumb

blocks.note: first meaning: a four-sided figure

blocks.clueFragment: a bone in the base of the thumb
blocks.note: second meaning: a small wrist bone

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a bone's shape; in fact both halves name the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: It names a quadrilateral with one pair of parallel sides, and also a carpal bone at the thumb's root.

clue.text: Poor, poor Santa! No thanks from singer

indicators.note: poor here means in a bad way, so the letters are knocked into disorder
no says the following item is left out of the fodder

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
ta is British slang for thank you; these letters are removed

explanation.surface: Poor Father Christmas gets no thanks from a carol singer.
explanation.walkthrough: The first Poor is the indicator; the second is fodder. Remove TA from POOR SANTA, then rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A soprano is a singer with the highest vocal range.

clue.text: I've followed a user; it's habit-forming

indicators.note: followed means coming after, so the first word is placed behind the second

blocks.note: a drug user is an addict
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to trailing a drug user, a compulsive habit.
explanation.definitionFit: Something addictive causes dependence, so it creates a habit that is hard to break.

clue.text: Exile's not in list of players

blocks.note: out is the opposite of in
the cast is the list of actors in a show

explanation.surface: An actor in exile is dropped from the company's cast list.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcast is someone rejected and driven away by society, like an exile.

clue.text: Nature's rages

blocks.note: first meaning: a person's characters or dispositions
second meaning: fits of anger

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as nature raging, like a storm; in fact two senses of one plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A temper is a person's disposition, and losing one's temper means a burst of anger.

clue.text: Commendation for lord, reportedly found in mine

indicators.note: reportedly means as said aloud by others, so the word is taken by its sound
found in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: laud, meaning praise, is said like lord in a non-rhotic accent
a pit is a coal mine

explanation.surface: A nobleman found down a mine earns praise.
explanation.walkthrough: The homophone works in a non-rhotic British accent, where lord and laud are said identically.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaudit is an expression of praise or approval, which is what a commendation is.

clue.text: Remedy for parent with a cane that's crooked

indicators.note: crooked means bent out of line, so the letters are twisted into a new order

blocks.note: pa is an informal word for father
the letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A parent leans on a bent walking stick as a cure.
explanation.definitionFit: A panacea is a supposed cure-all, a remedy for every ill.

clue.text: The American guy's a politician

blocks.note: the States is a common name for the USA
a guy is a man

explanation.surface: An American fellow turns out to be a politician.
explanation.definitionFit: A statesman is a respected, experienced political leader.

clue.text: Foolish, as in a sanctimonious hush

blocks.note: taken as written
pi is British slang for pious or sanctimonious
sh is the sound used to ask for quiet

explanation.surface: A smug, pious silence makes someone look silly.
explanation.definitionFit: Apish means silly or imitative, behaving like an ape in a foolish way.

clue.text: Regret going round the church, one gathered

indicators.note: going round means one piece surrounds the other

blocks.note: to rue is to regret
CH is the standard abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: Someone feels sorry walking round the church where a congregation met.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruche is a frill of fabric that has been gathered or pleated, so it is something gathered.

clue.text: Reversed guideline for the chief

blocks.note: a rule is a guideline
R marks reverse on a gear stick

explanation.surface: A rule turned on its head to suit the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: Reversed does not turn anything round here; R is the reverse-gear marking, placed after RULE.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruler is a sovereign or leader, the one in charge.

clue.text: Arabian Nights' character loses a graduate and has one excuse

indicators.note: loses means some letters are taken away from the character's name

blocks.note: Ali Baba of the forty thieves
taken as written; removed
a Bachelor of Arts; removed
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A storybook hero drops out of college and makes one excuse.
explanation.walkthrough: Take A and BA out of ALI BABA to leave ALIB, then add I.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is a claim of being elsewhere, used as an excuse or defence.

clue.text: Does better before ten on the right cry: "Onward and upward!"

blocks.note: to excel is to do better
I and O look like the digits of ten
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone improves just before ten and shouts encouragement.
explanation.walkthrough: Excelsior is the New York state motto and the title of a Longfellow poem.
explanation.definitionFit: Excelsior is Latin for 'higher', used as a rallying motto urging ever upward progress.

clue.text: Re bathers: arm one new river safety measure

indicators.note: new suggests a fresh version, so the letters are made into something different

blocks.note: the letters of these words
taken as written
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A notice about swimmers: arm each one anew.
explanation.walkthrough: The Thames Barrier is the movable flood defence across the River Thames in London.
explanation.definitionFit: The barrier closes to protect London from tidal flooding, a flood defence built across the river.
